Subject: QuantaOps capacity probe — starting the pre-sales sizing conversation

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this — we are kicking a new conversational product into pilot and need dedicated capacity estimates so we can evaluate reserved commitments. High-level context:

- Primary workload: multi-turn chat + occasional semantic-search/embeddings (chat ~80% traffic).
- Expected pilot peak: ~150–220 RPS sustained for short bursts (10–30 minutes).
- Typical session: user prompt ~= 200–400 tokens, model response ~= 800–1400 tokens (long-form summaries).
- Average concurrent sessions during peak: we estimate 3.5k sessions active (ballpark).
- Desired latency SLO: p95 generation latency <= 800ms for short responses, tolerated up to ~2.5s for long summaries.

Attached a 7-day telemetry snippet and a few workload snippets (quantaops_telemetry_sample.jsonl, quantaops_workload_snippets.txt) — they include timestamps, prompt token counts, response token counts, and a simple session id.

We'd like a short intake/worksheet from Redwood to capture burst windows, token mix, and any session-affinity requirements so you can recommend GPU sku mix and occupancy. Can you send the brief questionnaire or an intake form?

Thanks,
Cora
Cora Mills
Head of Platform, QuantaOps

Hi Cora — thanks for the telemetry, that’s very helpful. I attached our short capacity probe workbook (redwood_capacity_probe_form.xlsx) — it’s intentionally compact so we can get to a first-pass GPU mix quickly. A couple of clarifying asks we need filled in (quick bullets you can reply inline):

- Burst windows: what are the canonical burst durations you expect (10–30 minutes vs sustained 2–6 hours)?
- Peak RPS definition: is the 150–220 number per endpoint (chat API) or aggregated across many endpoints?
- Token distribution: can you provide the percentile token sizes (p50/p90/p99) for both prompts and responses if available?
- Session lifecycle: average session duration and whether sessions require KV-cache affinity (sticky to same machine) or can be stateless between turns.
- Multi-model routing: do you plan to route to smaller models for quick responses and larger models for summaries, and what fraction of traffic is expected to fall into each bucket?
- Regulatory/retention: do you need dedicated on-prem/private deployment or is hosted Dedicated acceptable?

I’ve looped in Karthik (pre-sales model fit) and Logan (capacity planner) — Karthik will take the lead on quantization/latency tradeoffs, Logan will run the occupancy/queue simulations once we have the p95 token mix.

Proposed next step: once you return the workbook, we’ll schedule a 30-minute walk-through to go over the telemetry and a preliminary sizing. Wednesday or Thursday next week works for us.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Neha — thanks for the quick turnaround. I filled the workbook and attached a more detailed snippet: quantaops_telemetry_sample.jsonl (7-day) — the file includes fields: ts, session_id, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, route (chat/search), and user_tier. Answers inline below: 

- Burst windows: historically we see 10–45 minute microbursts (majority) but we also have rarer multi-hour marketing events (1–4 hours) where sustained RPS is ~40% of the microburst peak.
- Peak RPS: 150–220 is aggregated across our public chat endpoints (single logical endpoint).
- Token percentiles (7d sample):
  - prompt tokens p50=220, p90=480, p99=1024
  - response tokens p50=680, p90=1200, p99=2400
- Session lifecycle: avg session length ~4.2 turns (~3–5 minutes). We prefer session affinity for KV-cache due to multi-turn context and to reduce repeated prompt sizes — affinity is strongly preferred but we can tolerate some cross-machine fallbacks for burst scaling.
- Multi-model routing: currently ~70% routed to a 13B variant for latency-sensitive replies, ~30% to a 34B variant for long summaries.
- Retention: hosted Dedicated is fine for pilot; may evaluate Private later for compliance.

If useful, I also attached a short extract of worst-case long responses and a synthetic day with an artificial marketing spike. Let me know if you want us to pull larger windows or full p95/p99 latency traces.

Best,
Cora

  2) an optimized plan (higher quantization, slightly higher p95 but lower $/token).
